title: the 319 PInputs semantic-name initialisers, one row per member
heading: ## Per-member rows: which node each of the semantic-name initialisers registers (OPUS, 2026-10-03)
lead: The family `PInputs semantic-name-registry initialisers` (frontmatter, {N} members) shares one 32-byte shape, stated here once and not repeated per row: `lea rcx, [node]` at + 0x4, a call to its registry's insert (section 2), `lea rcx, [teardown]`, and a tail jump to the CRT atexit registrar `00808B90`. What differs from member to member is the node that + 0x4 `lea` loads (and with it the name the node carries at qword `+0x8`, the key the insert compares), the insert called at + 0xB (one of five, the grouping below), and the teardown that + 0x10 `lea` hands to `00808B90` (each member has its own node-unlink teardown, listed in the members TSV's `dtor` column). The rows anchor the node `lea`; they do not state the teardown. Each row below anchors that `lea` (the member's distinguishing instruction) and states its node and the registered name. {CHECK} derives every row from the certified image and compares it with the committed {ROWS}: a member whose body leaves the shape, a node that differs or a name that differs fails it (two controls, a swapped node and a moved anchor, are refused). These rows explain which name each initialiser registers. They follow SWE2-AUDIT-SPEC's ruling on per-member rows (`202e59a0a`): the shared shape earns nothing, and only the distinguishing anchor with its value counts.
